A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same semantic collapsing problem (SCP) and Test-time Embedding Adjustment (TEA) work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original embedding-drift experiments, multi-concept analyses, hyperparameter studies and TEA evaluations on CC101 and CelebA.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds ClassDiffusion, EasyControl, ReVersion and Anti-DreamBooth experiments.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same normalization and spherical interpolation procedure, applied to token embeddings for Textual Inversion and contextualized prompt embeddings for DreamBooth. Equations 1–2 remain unchanged; the added applications do not document a new TEA component.

E1.justification: The original CC101 and CelebA coverage is retained. v2 adds Relationship tasks involving 'carved by', 'inside' and 'painted on' (Table 2), plus personalization using adversarially masked reference images. These introduce distinct task requirements and training-input conditions.

E2.justification: v2 retains Textual Inversion, DreamBooth and Custom Diffusion, adds ClassDiffusion to the CC101/CelebA comparisons, and evaluates EasyControl and ReVersion with and without TEA (Tables 1–2 and 6–7). These are participating comparators, not merely additional citations.

E3.justification: v2 adds Flux-based EasyControl evaluation and controlled Anti-DreamBooth experiments varying masked-image proportions and TEA adjustment settings. The original Stable Diffusion settings remain documented unchanged. The intermediate masking condition is uncertain: Section 4.2 specifies 20%, whereas Figure 7 labels it 25%.

E4.justification: v2 adds poisoning-induced drift analysis and rotation-versus-scaling sensitivity tests for Anti-DreamBooth (Figures 7–8 and 13–14), plus failure-case comparisons for the added methods. The original multi-concept and hyperparameter analyses are retained and moved into Appendices B and C.1.

E5.justification: New Figures 28–30 explicitly report using the same random seed for baseline/TEA qualitative comparisons. The existing 100-seed and 50-run averages and rotation-ablation ± reporting remain unchanged. No increase in repeated runs or new statistical inference procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds ClassDiffusion scores, EasyControl/ReVersion results and qualitative recovery findings under poisoning. For example, its new EasyControl dog comparison reports CLIP-I of 61.33 without TEA and 64.56 with TEA; ReVersion 'carved by' reports full-prompt CLIP scores of 27.74 and 30.17. Retained TI, DreamBooth and Custom Diffusion table entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a constrained bilevel formulation of anti-personalization and a reconstruction/prior-loss expression (v2 Equations 6–7). These extend the mathematical background. Existing TEA equations and distance definitions remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2 introduces counteracting Anti-DreamBooth as a fourth contribution and highlights it in the introduction and conclusion, claiming partial recovery of protected concepts and an overlooked defense weakness. The original SCP diagnosis and training-free TEA contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets Anti-DreamBooth as amplifying semantic collapse and attributes recovery primarily to correcting embedding direction rather than magnitude (Section 4.2 and Appendix C.2). It removes v1's evaluation-limitations paragraph while retaining the prompt-versus-identity tradeoff and limitations of fixed hyperparameters.

D1.justification: The documented code and prompt access location changes from anonymous hosting to a named GitHub repository. A new LLM-use statement identifies ChatGPT among the tools used. Original GPU, batch-size, learning-rate and LoRA details are retained; detailed settings for the added pipelines remain sparse.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands discussion of anti-personalization, adversarial learning and concept erasure in Appendix A.2. Appendix A.3 adds explicit comparisons with PALP, LEGO and ReVersion, positioning TEA against training-time regularization and token-based personalization approaches.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites substantial introduction and evaluation prose, condenses the standalone personalization background into a terminology subsection, and moves the multi-concept and hyperparameter sections into appendices. The title, section hierarchy, citation style and narrative organization also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds a results teaser, a TEA framework schematic, Anti-DreamBooth plots and image grids, and qualitative displays for three added methods. It introduces the EasyControl/ReVersion table and expands existing comparison tables. Original figure images are retained, with several displays relocated and the rotation table relabeled as Figure 11.

improvement.justification: v2 materially strengthens evidence for TEA's broad applicability through a different architecture, relationship-personalization tasks and ClassDiffusion comparisons, addressing v1's explicitly acknowledged evaluation restriction. The controlled poisoning study and method schematic add explanatory value. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, although the 20%/25% masking discrepancy and Appendix F.3's unchanged claim that all experiments use Stable Diffusion v1.5 limit reproducibility of the expanded evaluation.
